cards.info: What is sampling bias?
cards.backInfo: Sampling bias occurs when the selection method results in a sample that does not represent the target population.

cards.info: What is undercoverage in survey design?
cards.backInfo: Undercoverage is sampling bias where specific population subgroups have no chance of being selected for the study.

cards.info: What is a sampling frame?
cards.backInfo: The sampling frame is the actual list or set of procedures used to select individuals for a sample.

cards.info: When does nonresponse bias occur?
cards.backInfo: It occurs when selected individuals who do not participate differ systematically from those who do participate.

cards.info: How is the response rate calculated?
cards.backInfo: Divide the number of respondents by the total number of individuals initially selected for the sample.

cards.info: What is a primary indicator of potential nonresponse bias?
cards.backInfo: A low response rate, often below 20%, is a major red flag for nonresponse bias.

cards.info: When does sampling bias occur compared to nonresponse bias?
cards.backInfo: Sampling bias occurs during the selection phase; nonresponse bias occurs during the participation phase after selection.

cards.info: How do you identify sampling bias in a study?
cards.backInfo: Check if any specific subgroups of the target population were excluded from the initial sampling frame.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps to identify sampling and nonresponse bias.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/1f792355-4bbe-4090-bb03-e181930349f0-1786506150745-994.webp)

cards.info: How do you identify nonresponse bias using demographics?
cards.backInfo: Compare the demographic characteristics of the respondents to those of the target population for systematic differences.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps to identify sampling and nonresponse bias.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/1f792355-4bbe-4090-bb03-e181930349f0-1786506150745-994.webp)

cards.info: Does a large sample size eliminate bias?
cards.backInfo: No; a large sample size cannot fix results if the underlying sampling frame was flawed or biased.

cards.info: If a researcher only surveys people at a luxury mall, what error occurs?
cards.backInfo: Sampling bias occurs because the selection method fails to represent the entire population.

cards.info: Using a phone book to select participants excludes those without landlines. Name this.
cards.backInfo: This is undercoverage, a form of sampling bias where a subgroup is excluded.

cards.info: What term describes the specific list used to contact potential survey participants?
cards.backInfo: The sampling frame is the actual list or procedure used to draw a sample.

cards.info: Why is it a problem if non-participants differ systematically from respondents?
cards.backInfo: This systematic difference creates nonresponse bias, making the survey results unrepresentative.

cards.info: A survey contacts 5,000 people and 400 respond. What is the denominator?
cards.backInfo: The denominator is 5,000, the total number of individuals selected for the sample.

cards.info: A study has an 8% response rate. What bias should you suspect?
cards.backInfo: A low response rate (below 20%) strongly suggests the presence of nonresponse bias.

cards.info: Which bias is an error in selection versus an error in participation?
cards.backInfo: Sampling bias is a selection error; nonresponse bias is a participation error.

cards.info: What is the first step of the Frame-and-Respond Check?
cards.backInfo: Identify the sampling frame and check if any subgroups were left out.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps to identify sampling and nonresponse bias.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/1f792355-4bbe-4090-bb03-e181930349f0-1786506150745-994.webp)

cards.info: Respondents are 80% homeowners, but the population is 60%. What is checked?
cards.backInfo: Demographic comparison is used here to identify the presence of nonresponse bias.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps to identify sampling and nonresponse bias.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/1f792355-4bbe-4090-bb03-e181930349f0-1786506150745-994.webp)

cards.info: Can a single study suffer from both sampling and nonresponse bias?
cards.backInfo: Yes, if the frame excludes subgroups and the response rate is low/skewed.
